chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Invited to England: tours with Buddy Tate, Dickie Wells and others
summary: Jack Higgins invited him to England, where he first brought his own band, and returned in 1961 with Sir Charles and Jimmy Witherspoon.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, it sure is. Then while I was in Belgium I got a call from Jack Higgins. (LAUGHTER). To ask if I would like to come to England and play with Humphrey Lyttleton. Yes, that was one of the main things I wanted to do because I had heard a lot about Humphrey. Even Louis used to tell me about Humphrey. Jimmy Rushing used to tell me about Humphrey.

So I told him yes, I'd love to. So the next year I went over there with my own band. I didn't join Humphrey right away. The next year I took, before George Weir, I took Buddy Tate and Earl Warren, Dickie Wells and Emmett Berry, Herbie Lovelle, Al Williams and who else? And Rush!
Gene Ramey. And on the bill with us was Dizzy and Dave Brubeck. So that was a nice trip. That was a good trip.
Yes that was a fairly well balanced trip.

Yes, that was a very good trip. And everybody, everything went okay. Then I went back again in '61 with almost the same guys except a different drummer. I had Oliver Jackson. When we didn't have Jimmy Rushing we had Witherspoon, Jimmy Witherspoon.
Did you take Sir Charles on that trip?

Yes. Sir Charles, yes. That was a fairly nice trip until it got kind of rough near the end because the bookings had been badly booked. Some of the dates were cut out and it wasn't as good, I don't think it was as good as the first one, you know.
As good a band but not as good ......
